correctness.rationale: The two-baseline residue lemma is proved bijectively. Because each a is odd, residues of b*y+c*z correspond to q=y+3z or q=2y+3z. Fixed-q cheapest pairs and all alternatives are exactly enumerated by a positive-cost substitution, and explicit f(q+a)-f(q) differences prevent omitted lower competitors. Exhaustive special-residue comparisons give both all-k quadratics with separate k=0 cases. A standalone two-route checker verified 72 complete parameters; finite tests are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The 2021 Robles-Pérez--Rosales paper introduces exactly the two prime-triplet templates, proves p=0 Apéry/genera/Frobenius results, and expressly proposes p-Frobenius as future work (Remark 2.4). Full relevant sections were read. Komatsu--Ying p-Frobenius formulas apply to arithmetic-progression triples (a,a+d,a+2d), not gap pairs (2,4) or (4,2). Liu--Xin develops ordinary p=0 Frobenius optimization, not thresholds with two representations. Targeted web and published-finding corpus searches did not reveal this two-family p=1 formula. Indexed absence cannot certify absolute novelty.

value.rationale: This directly addresses the first positive p-Frobenius layer in both prime-triplet template families, explicitly singled out for further work by Robles-Pérez--Rosales. Two infinite closed expressions and their exceptional small-parameter switch quantify the onset of duplicate representations, which cannot be read off the classical p=0 Frobenius/genera. Both branches are natural complete families rather than arbitrary finite slices; no statement for higher p is needed to make the first layer mathematically interpretable.
